title: Mission 15: The Time Capsule
story: Fiscal year end. Everything the department built gets sealed into archives for the records vault - and one mystery capsule from five years ago needs opening. tar bundles trees into single files; gzip crushes them small. Together they are how Linux ships, backs up and remembers.

badge.name: The Time Capsule: Sealed
badge.desc: Mastered tar and gzip by sealing, compressing, inspecting and reopening archives byte-perfectly.

tasks.brief: Read BRIEFING15.txt in your department directory. Seal the capsule/yearbook/ directory into a plain (uncompressed) tar archive: capsule/yearbook.tar, created FROM the capsule/ directory so the archive's paths start with yearbook/.

checks.fail: yearbook.tar does not contain exactly the yearbook/ tree with yearbook/-prefixed paths (create it from inside capsule/, naming the directory).

tasks.brief: The vault charges by the byte. Compress a COPY of your archive with gzip so BOTH exist: yearbook.tar (original) and yearbook_copy.tar.gz (compressed). (gzip normally replaces its input - copy first, or discover its keep option.)

checks.fail: yearbook_copy.tar.gz is not a valid gzip file (gzip -t tests integrity).
The original yearbook.tar vanished - gzip replaced it. Keep both (copy first, or gzip's -k).

tasks.brief: The pros do it in one move: create capsule/ledgers.tgz - the capsule/ledgers/ directory tarred AND gzip-compressed in a single tar command (the z flag), again with ledgers/-prefixed paths.

checks.fail: ledgers.tgz is not gzip-compressed (tar's z flag compresses while it seals).
ledgers.tgz does not contain exactly the ledgers/ tree (create from inside capsule/).

tasks.brief: NEVER extract blind. The mystery capsule capsule/mystery_2021.tgz arrived from records. LIST its contents without extracting and save that listing exactly to capsule/manifest.txt.

checks.fail: manifest.txt must be tar's listing of mystery_2021.tgz (the t flag lists; nothing lands on disk).

tasks.brief: Now open it: extract mystery_2021.tgz INTO the capsule/opened/ directory (tar can aim its extraction with -C). The 2021 files must land under opened/, nowhere else.

checks.fail: The 2021 files have not landed under capsule/opened/ yet (extract with -C opened).
deposits.txt came out corrupted - extraction must be byte-perfect.
The capsule spilled into capsule/ itself instead of opened/ (aim tar with -C).

tasks.brief: Records needs ONE file from the mystery capsule without a full unpack: extract ONLY vault_2021/note_to_future.txt straight to capsule/rescued/ (tar extracts named members; combine with -C).

checks.fail: note_to_future.txt has not been surgically extracted into rescued/ (name the member after the archive; aim with -C).
More than the named file came out - this was a single-member rescue.
The yearbook source tree changed. Archiving photographs the room; it does not rearrange it.
The mystery capsule itself is gone. Originals return to the vault after opening.

tasks.brief: BONUS: how small did gzip crush the yearbook? gzip -l reads a .gz file's compression stats. From its output for yearbook_copy.tar.gz, write just the UNCOMPRESSED byte count to capsule/truesize.txt.

checks.fail: truesize.txt must contain the uncompressed size gzip -l reports for yearbook_copy.tar.gz (that number equals the original .tar's byte count).
